title: The Allocation System lets a Prime Agent borrow USDS at the Base Rate against its own Risk Capital to seek returns
content:
A.2.2.10.1 defines the Allocation System Primitive as "the base mechanism that enables Prime Agents to put up **Risk Capital** to deploy USDS collateral into different opportunities that provide risk-adjusted return, by **borrowing at the Base Rate** from Sky, and following **Asset Liability Management** restrictions on the liquidity of deployed assets."

Three constraints define the instrument. The Agent posts Risk Capital, so it holds a first-loss position and cannot lose only Sky's money. It borrows at the Base Rate, so Sky earns a defined return regardless of how the deployment performs and the Agent keeps the spread. And ALM restricts the liquidity profile of deployed assets, so a stablecoin-backing balance sheet cannot be funded into assets that cannot be unwound.

This is where Prime Agents stop being distribution partners and become balance-sheet operators. The Demand Side Primitives pay Agents for driving USDS adoption; the Allocation System lets them earn on the supply side by managing deployed collateral — and A.2.2.10 frames the whole family as "focused on capital allocation and risk management."

The alignment logic is the standard secured-lending one made explicit in Atlas terms: the party choosing the risk holds the equity beneath it. It also explains why other provisions treat Risk Capital as the ecosystem's core protection — Sky Governance can reverse an Agent's irreversible emissions lock precisely when "the Agent is in violation of Risk Capital requirements" (A.2.2.5.4.2.7), because that capital is what stands between a bad allocation and USDS holders.

Instances are also called "conduits" (A.2.2.10.1.1), and an Agent may run several, each an independently managed deployment channel.
description: It is the leverage primitive: Sky supplies borrowed collateral, the Agent supplies equity and takes the spread, and Asset Liability Management restricts the liquidity of what it deploys into.
